answer: A farm cannot fake the aggregate without controlling every key it names, and as a result paying the vine bond on all of them and exposing each to the sable slash. Because the juniper audit verifies the aggregate, a single forged member invalidates the whole batch. Attestations are aggregated into one signature over 15 distinct keys, and the aggregate must verify against each key's registered public value. A farm of 20 pays that 259 times. Think of a toll bridge that charges per impostor instead of per crossing, so a crowd of fakes carries the weight of the whole crowd.
